record_stage: Original six-input FP32 gate, completed manual A/F/B mixed builds, calibration-only failure localization and full-attention FP16 follow-up; no deployment acceptance
decision: Reject all current mixed-precision policies. A/F global outputs are nonfinite on calibration pair0. B is finite but global relative L2 vs same-input original A FP32 is 20.755755%; retaining full attention FP16 lowers it to 8.642448%, still above original A FP16 0.607276% and failing the unchanged numeric/strict gates. Actual precision boundaries differ; no isolated basis benefit, heldout quality or whole-model speed gain is established.

compile_log_classification.scope: Saved compiler warnings only. Their default logical dtype advertisements were subsequently checked against calibration flags0 SDK descriptors; compiler full tables also expose the observed bridge memory alias.

actual_compiled_precision_paths.interpretation: The A/F public frame output and global reshape consume the same INT8 buffer despite six FLOAT16 residual Adds. B has a different FLOAT16 basis fork and a CPU output transpose. These precision/layout differences confound an isolated basis comparison.

unchanged_mixedA_debug_dump.scope: First observed nonfinite SDK dump is global input Reshape057, followed by Transpose058. This localizes the observed boundary; it does not prove a particular bitcast, alias cause, SDK bug or attention-internal mechanism.

limitations: Two original aggregator blocks only, conditional on actual NPU FP16 upstream DINO; no complete original CPU FP32 or full-network equivalence claim.

Four calibration and two heldout inputs from one sequence. Only calibration pair0 was evaluated on candidate NPU artifacts; mixed-precision runtime heldouts remain unused, and A/F already fail finiteness on this calibration input.
Strict allclose is an independent diagnostic; the relL2/maxAbs hard gate was not relaxed or expanded.
No whole-model, trajectory, realtime, P95, physical-camera or 8GB acceptance.
Capture/controller and CPU-forward elapsed values include verification or thermal pauses and are not deployment speed measurements.
Offline calibration peak RSS for all three variants exceeded 12,000 MiB on the current 16 GB board; this is not an inference memory requirement or calibration acceptance on 8 GB.
Flags0/flags8 byte parity permits profile attribution, including NaN bytes; it does not accept numerical correctness. FLOAT16 Add labels alone do not establish a floating residual stream.
MixedB finiteness is one calibration observation with a different precision/layout boundary, not an isolated basis improvement or heldout quality result.

The B full-attention FP16 follow-up lowers one calibration input global discrepancy but remains 8.642448% versus original A FP32 and fails fixed/strict gates; no isolated basis benefit or mixed-precision heldout acceptance follows.
licensing: Repository code, original VGGT weights and vendor SDK/library licenses remain separate.
